scenes.tts: Each step has two strokes. The centrosome moves ahead, then the nucleus catches up. But what makes it catch up?
scenes.visual: Title card: What Brings the Nucleus Up. A bipolar neuron with its centrosome dot ahead of the nucleus disc.
scenes.narration: Each step has two strokes. The centrosome moves ahead, then the nucleus catches up. But what makes it catch up?

scenes.tts: Inside the cell, bundles of microtubules wrap the nucleus like a cage. They run forward to the centrosome.
scenes.visual: Close-up: microtubule bundles wrap the nucleus and converge on the centrosome ahead of it. Label: cage seen by electron microscopy in fixed anterior-SVZ neuroblasts from newborn rats (Schaar and McConnell, 2005). Corner tag for the rest of the chapter: schematic model combining that work with rat cortical-slice imaging.
scenes.narration: Inside the cell, bundles of microtubules wrap the nucleus like a cage. They run forward to the centrosome.

scenes.tts: Microtubules have a direction. In the usual picture, their minus ends gather at the centrosome. Their plus ends point away from it.
scenes.visual: Minus signs appear at the centrosome; plus signs at the rear of the cage and out in the leading process.
scenes.narration: Microtubules have a direction. In the usual picture, their minus ends gather at the centrosome. Their plus ends point away from it.

scenes.tts: The motor is dye-neen. It walks toward minus ends, that is, toward the centrosome.
scenes.caption: The motor is dynein. It walks toward minus ends, that is, toward the centrosome.
scenes.visual: A dynein motor steps along a microtubule toward the minus end. Label: cytoplasmic dynein walks toward minus ends.
scenes.narration: The motor is dynein. It walks toward minus ends, that is, toward the centrosome.

scenes.tts: What dye-neen moves depends on what holds it.
scenes.caption: What dynein moves depends on what holds it.
scenes.visual: Two panels open side by side, labelled: held in place; attached to something that can move.
scenes.narration: What dynein moves depends on what holds it.

scenes.tts: If dye-neen is held in place, it cannot walk. So it drags the microtubule instead, and the centrosome comes toward it.
scenes.caption: If dynein is held in place, it cannot walk. So it drags the microtubule instead, and the centrosome comes toward it.
scenes.visual: Panel A: a dynein held by a schematic anchor, marked proposed, inside the leading-process swelling. The microtubule slides past it, and the centrosome at its minus end advances toward the dynein.
scenes.narration: If dynein is held in place, it cannot walk. So it drags the microtubule instead, and the centrosome comes toward it.

scenes.tts: If dye-neen rides on something that can move, it carries that thing toward the centrosome.
scenes.caption: If dynein rides on something that can move, it carries that thing toward the centrosome.
scenes.visual: Panel B: a dynein riding on a disc carries the disc along the microtubule toward the minus end.
scenes.narration: If dynein rides on something that can move, it carries that thing toward the centrosome.

scenes.tts: In the usual model, a neuron uses both. In stroke one, dye-neen in the swelling pulls the microtubules forward. The centrosome comes with them.
scenes.caption: In the usual model, a neuron uses both. In stroke one, dynein in the swelling pulls the microtubules forward. The centrosome comes with them.
scenes.visual: Back to the neuron. Dynein marks glow in the swelling; the microtubule network and the centrosome slide forward into it. Label: stroke one.
scenes.narration: In the usual model, a neuron uses both. In stroke one, dynein in the swelling pulls the microtubules forward. The centrosome comes with them.

scenes.tts: In stroke two, dye-neen on the nucleus walks along the cage. It carries the nucleus toward the centrosome, which now sits ahead.
scenes.caption: In stroke two, dynein on the nucleus walks along the cage. It carries the nucleus toward the centrosome, which now sits ahead.
scenes.visual: Dynein marks glow on the nuclear envelope; the disc moves forward toward the dot. Label: stroke two.
scenes.narration: In stroke two, dynein on the nucleus walks along the cage. It carries the nucleus toward the centrosome, which now sits ahead.

scenes.tts: L I S one binds dye-neen and regulates it in both places. It is not the motor itself.
scenes.caption: LIS1 binds dynein and regulates it in both places. It is not the motor itself.
scenes.visual: LIS1 tags appear at both dynein sites. Label: LIS1 binds and regulates dynein; it is not the motor.
scenes.narration: LIS1 binds dynein and regulates it in both places. It is not the motor itself.

scenes.tts: A second force comes from actin and myosin two. A drug called blebbistatin blocks myosin two.
scenes.caption: A second force comes from actin and myosin II. A drug called blebbistatin blocks myosin II.
scenes.visual: A schematic actomyosin icon appears with a question mark, at no fixed place in the cell (its location is still argued). Label: blebbistatin blocks myosin II.
scenes.narration: A second force comes from actin and myosin II. A drug called blebbistatin blocks myosin II.

scenes.tts: Now the experiment, in slices of embryonic rat cortex. Label the centrosome and the nucleus, and film the neurons.
scenes.visual: Three side-by-side movies, labelled: control; LIS1 or dynein knocked down; blebbistatin. Caption: slices of embryonic rat cortex. A table frame appears: tip, centrosome, nucleus.
scenes.narration: Now the experiment, in slices of embryonic rat cortex. Label the centrosome and the nucleus, and film the neurons.

scenes.tts: Knock down L I S one, or block myosin two. What do the tip, the centrosome and the nucleus each do?
scenes.caption: Knock down LIS1, or block myosin II. What do the tip, the centrosome and the nucleus each do?
scenes.visual: The table cells are blank. Caption: Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: Knock down LIS1, or block myosin II. What do the tip, the centrosome and the nucleus each do?

scenes.tts: Knock down L I S one or dye-neen, and the centrosome stalls. The nucleus stalls too. But the tip keeps growing.
scenes.caption: Knock down LIS1 or dynein, and the centrosome stalls. The nucleus stalls too. But the tip keeps growing.
scenes.visual: Knockdown movie: the dot and the disc freeze while the tip grows. Table row fills: keeps extending, stalls, stalls. Caption: slices of embryonic rat cortex; other cell types differ.
scenes.narration: Knock down LIS1 or dynein, and the centrosome stalls. The nucleus stalls too. But the tip keeps growing.

scenes.tts: Block myosin two, and the centrosome keeps moving. The nucleus stops, so the gap between them grows.
scenes.caption: Block myosin II, and the centrosome keeps moving. The nucleus stops, so the gap between them grows.
scenes.visual: Blebbistatin movie: the dot runs ahead while the disc stays; a bracket shows the gap widening. Table row fills: keeps extending, keeps moving, stops.
scenes.narration: Block myosin II, and the centrosome keeps moving. The nucleus stops, so the gap between them grows.

scenes.tts: Dye-neen's pull on the centrosome is still there. But the nucleus has lost a force it needs.
scenes.caption: Dynein's pull on the centrosome is still there. But the nucleus has lost a force it needs.
scenes.visual: The swelling dynein still glows; the label myosin II is greyed out.
scenes.narration: Dynein's pull on the centrosome is still there. But the nucleus has lost a force it needs.

scenes.tts: Exactly where myosin two acts, behind the nucleus or at the front, is still argued.
scenes.caption: Exactly where myosin II acts, behind the nucleus or at the front, is still argued.
scenes.visual: Two arrows, one squeezing from behind the nucleus and one pulling from the front, both with question marks.
scenes.narration: Exactly where myosin II acts, behind the nucleus or at the front, is still argued.

scenes.tts: So a cell can keep reaching without arriving. Measure migration at the nucleus.
scenes.visual: Closing card: A cell can keep reaching without arriving. Measure at the nucleus.
scenes.narration: So a cell can keep reaching without arriving. Measure migration at the nucleus.
